title: Pelvic inflammatory disease and female genital tuberculosis: pathogenesis, tubo-ovarian abscess and Asherman syndrome
subject: ss-obg
refs: Gynecology by Ten Teachers 21e Ch 14 (Pelvic infection and STIs)
CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines (2021)
Index-TB Guidelines on extrapulmonary tuberculosis in India (WHO/CTD)

steps.say: Pelvic inflammatory disease begins as an ascending sexually transmitted endocervical infection that spreads into upper genital structures. Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae breach the endocervical barrier, initiating purulent salpingitis, endometritis, and pelvic peritonitis.
steps.tx: The pathogenesis of **pelvic inflammatory disease** (PID) involves ascending mucosal infection by **Chlamydia trachomatis** and **Neisseria gonorrhoeae**, which disrupt the endocervical barrier and ascend into the endometrium and fallopian tubes, provoking acute **purulent salpingitis**, fimbrial edema, endometritis, and pelvic peritonitis.

vis.caption: Ascending mucosal infection, tubal deciliation, and pelvic peritonitis. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Pathophysiological diagram of ascending STI progression to salpingitis and abscess.

steps.say: Clinical diagnosis of acute pelvic inflammatory disease relies on standardized clinical criteria to prevent delayed treatment. Empiric antimicrobial therapy is mandated when pelvic examination reveals uterine tenderness, adnexal tenderness, or cervical motion tenderness in sexually active women.
steps.tx: According to CDC criteria, empiric therapy for PID is initiated in sexually active young women presenting with pelvic pain if at least one minimum clinical sign is present: **cervical motion tenderness** (Chandelier sign), **uterine tenderness**, or **adnexal tenderness** on bimanual pelvic examination.

rows: Cervical motion, uterine, or adnexal tenderness
Oral temp > 38.3 C, abnormal mucopurulent discharge
Enhances diagnostic specificity for acute PID
Elevated CRP, ESR, positive cervical NAAT for GC/CT
Confirms severe complicated PID or abscess

steps.say: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome arises from transperitoneal or lymphatic spread of acute pelvic infection to the liver capsule. Patients develop perihepatitis manifesting as severe right upper quadrant pleuritic pain, revealing pathognomonic violin-string adhesions on laparoscopy.
steps.tx: **Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome** represents perihepatitis complicating acute Chlamydia or gonococcal pelvic infection. Acute inflammation of Glisson's capsule causes sharp **right upper quadrant pain** mimicking acute cholecystitis, with laparoscopy demonstrating pathognomonic **violin-string adhesions** spanning between the anterior liver capsule and abdominal wall.

left.title: Clinical Presentation of Perihepatitis
points: Severe pleuritic right upper quadrant pain referred to right shoulder
Normal or mildly elevated serum transaminases and bilirubin
Frequently misdiagnosed as acute cholecystitis or pleurisy

right.title: Diagnostic & Laparoscopic Findings
points: Exudative capsular inflammation during acute stage
Chronic healing leaves fibrous 'violin-string' peritoneal adhesions
Rapid symptomatic resolution with standard parenteral PID antibiotics

steps.say: Parenteral therapy for acute complicated pelvic inflammatory disease requires broad-spectrum anaerobic and atypical antimicrobial coverage. The CDC parenteral protocol administers intravenous ceftriaxone at one gram every twenty-four hours, oral or IV doxycycline at 100 milligrams twice daily, and oral or IV metronidazole.
steps.tx: First-line inpatient parenteral treatment for acute PID consists of **intravenous ceftriaxone** (1 g IV every 24 hours) plus oral or IV **doxycycline** (100 mg every 12 hours) and **metronidazole** (500 mg every 12 hours) to ensure comprehensive broad-spectrum anaerobic and atypical coverage.

nodes.label: Establish indication for hospitalization (pregnancy, TOA, severe illness, nausea)
Administer IV ceftriaxone 1 g q24h + doxycycline 100 mg q12h + metronidazole 500 mg q12h
Monitor for clinical defervescence and reduction of pelvic peritonism
Transition to oral doxycycline and metronidazole after 24 to 48 hours of improvement

steps.say: A tubo-ovarian abscess represents a severe, suppurative complication of upper pelvic infection. Adnexal architecture becomes disorganized into a complex, multilocular inflammatory mass with thickened walls and internal echogenic debris on transvaginal ultrasound.
steps.tx: A **tubo-ovarian abscess** (TOA) represents end-stage suppurative pelvic infection. Sonography demonstrates a complex, multilocular, thick-walled adnexal mass containing internal **echogenic debris**. Initial management involves parenteral broad-spectrum antibiotics, with **percutaneous drainage** indicated if the abscess measures >= 8 cm or fails to resolve.

rows: Medium to large TOA (5 to 8 cm)
IV antibiotics plus ultrasound-guided needle aspiration
Life-saving peritoneal toilet and source control

steps.say: Female genital tuberculosis arises almost exclusively via hematogenous dissemination from an active or dormant pulmonary or abdominal primary focus. The fallopian tubes are involved bilaterally in nearly one hundred percent of cases, followed by the endometrium in fifty to sixty percent.
steps.tx: **Genital tuberculosis** in women occurs via hematogenous or lymphatic dissemination of *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*. The **fallopian tubes** are involved bilaterally in nearly **100 percent of cases**, followed by the endometrium in 50 to 60 percent, causing primary or secondary infertility and irreversible tubal damage.

left.title: Tubal Involvement (95-100%)
points: Always bilateral; leads to rigid 'pipestem' or 'lead-pipe' tubes
Fimbrial eversion without occlusion ('tobacco pouch' deformity)
Calcified pelvic lymph nodes and peritubal caseating granulomas

right.title: Endometrial Involvement (50-60%)
points: Direct spread from infected fallopian tubal mucosa
Caseous destruction leads to dense fibrotic intrauterine synechiae
Manifests as hypomenorrhoea, oligomenorrhoea, and secondary amenorrhoea

steps.say: Chronic caseous destruction of the endometrium culminates in secondary amenorrhoea and irreversible infertility. Fibrous obliteration of the uterine cavity produces tuberculous Asherman syndrome, appearing on fluoroscopy as a small, contracted cavity with jagged filling defects.
steps.tx: Tuberculous endometritis causes destruction of the basal endometrial layer and dense intrauterine synechiae, termed **tuberculous Asherman syndrome**. Hysterosalpingography reveals a small, shrunken cavity with irregular jagged borders, termed **golf-club appearance** or **accordion uterus**, presenting with intractable hypomenorrhoea and secondary amenorrhoea.

nodes.label: Mycobacterium tuberculosis reaches endometrium via descending tubal flow
Caseating granulomatous inflammation obliterates basal regenerative layer
Dense fibrotic synechiae obliterate the uterine cavity (Asherman syndrome)
Presents with intractable secondary amenorrhoea unresponsive to estrogen

steps.say: Diagnosing female genital tuberculosis requires molecular and histological demonstration of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Endometrial tissue biopsy obtained during the premenstrual phase confirms diagnosis through GeneXpert PCR, positive mycobacterial cultures, or characteristic caseating granulomas on histopathology.
steps.tx: Definitive diagnosis of female genital TB requires **endometrial biopsy** performed in the premenstrual phase, evaluated by **GeneXpert MTB/RIF**, mycobacterial culture on Lowenstein-Jensen medium, and histopathological identification of classic **caseating epithelioid granulomas** with Langhans giant cells surrounded by a peripheral lymphocytic collar.
